caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1703 of 2010
lawyer:
Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. N. I. Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Md. Mazibur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondents
parties:
Md. Amzad Hossain Parag ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Saiful Islam and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 16. In this suit the plaintiff has prayed for a decree declaring a registered deed of the year 1975 as forged, inoperative and collusive. A registered deed has got a presumptive value of being genuine. This presumption no doubt, rebuttable. The party who claims a registered deed to be forged, collusive etc. the initial .onus upon that party to prove that the said registered deed is actually forged and collusive. But in this suit it appears that the plaintiff has failed to discharge this onus. The plaintiff has examined two witnesses only including himself. The trial court has discussed the evidence of these two P.Ws. in his judgment and opined rightly that the plaintiff could not adduce any evidence to prove that the impugned registered deed is forged. The trial court has considered the evidence of defendant No. 12-the executor of the impugned registered deed who was examined on commission as D.W.4. The trial court has quoted some portion of the evidence of this D.W.4 in its judgment. This D.W.4 in. cross-examination has stated that his nayeb Ahmad Ali Pramanik used to negotiate the transfers of land by him and in many cases he took the consideration money also from the purchasers. This D.W.4 has stated also that he could not remember how much land he sold and by how many deeds in the year 1975. It appears that the trial court has deeply considered the evidence of this D.W.4 who was an old man of 76 years and rightly opined that in view of the evidence of this D.W.4 it could not he held that he did not execute the impugned deed. The trial court has examined and compared the signatures of this D.W. 4 in the impugned kabala deed with his signatures in a registered kabala deed of the year 1976-the exhibit 'Ka 1' executed by this D.W.4 as per section 73 of the Evidence Act and found that both the signatures are similar. The appellate court below, of course, has made comment to the effect that this exhibit 1 ' had not been proved genuine in accordance with law. But it appears that the plaintiff-petitioner did not raise any objection as to genuineness of this exhibit-'Ka 1. In this leave petition there is no statement or submission at all questioning the genuineness of this old registered deed the exhibit Ka 1'. However, it appears that both the appellate court below and the revisional court held a very erroneous view that in this suit the onus was entirely on the contesting defendants to prove that the impugned kabala deed was a genuine one. This view of the appellate court and the High Court Division is wrong. The burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lies on that person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side. In this present suit the plaintiff sought a decree declaring an old registered kabala deed collusive, fraudulent etc. In this suit if no evidence is given from either side the suit will fail and consequently the impugned kabala deed will stand valid. In the circumstances the initial onus was on the plaintiff to prove his allegation that this registered deed was forged and collusive etc. But it appears that, as I have already mentioned above, the plaintiff has miserably failed to discharge this onus. The plaintiff did not pray even to the trial court to examine the signatures of the defendant No. 12 in the impugned kabala deed with his some admitted signatures by a handwriting expert in order to prove the alleged forgery in creating the impugned kabala deed.
